title: Orbit
suits: planetary or networked products: climate, logistics, satellites and data, global payments, connectivity. Tod 0.5 is the hero frame for a vision slide. Not for intimate or playful products.

params.data-tod: 0…1, where the sun is: 0 the day side (sun glint on the oceans), 0.5 the terminator crossing the view with a sunset band on the limb, 1 the night side (city lights, airglow, aurora)
params.data-seed: integer; another planet (continents, clouds, cities). Keep one seed across a deck
params.data-print-t: clock time of the still frame for print (default 40)
params.--brand / --brand-2 on the section: optional: the aurora's rays take --brand, their tops --brand-2 (default green and magenta)

details: the ground drifts slowly toward the horizon, as it does under a real orbit; clouds and coastlines slide under the limb
the terminator moves with tod; along it the ground warms to rose and the limb turns orange, then red, where the sunset is
on the night side, city lights cluster along the coasts and stay hidden under thick cloud
a thin green airglow line floats just above the limb on the night side, with a dark gap under it, as in ISS photos
the sun glints on the oceans on the day side; the glint skips over land and cloud
lightning flickers inside night-side storms: two quick strokes, then a fade
an aurora sliver stands on the limb toward the pole at night: soft green rays that fold and travel, magenta at the tops
a meteor burns up below you once a minute, a short green streak inside the atmosphere, not across the stars
five satellites cross on different inclinations; one carries a faint imaging swath behind it
one satellite flares once mid-pass (an antenna catching the sun), then fades back to a point
a spent rocket stage tumbles, so its light pulses as it crosses
at night the satellites slide into Earth's shadow and go out mid-sky
the station drifts across the right third; a solar panel glints every 11 s and its red and green nav lights blink
on the night side the station is in Earth's shadow: a dark silhouette with only its nav lights
fewer stars by day (the bright Earth stops the exposure down), the full field and a faint Milky Way with a dust lane by night
space is deep indigo and violet with faint nebula tints, never black; film grain over everything
